correctness.rationale: The precise claim is for countably infinitely many genuine closed real arcs of positive lengths with L=inf ell_n>0. The edge-derivative dual consists exactly of uniformly bounded L-infinity families with common integral; its annihilator inside the ell1 sum of L1(I_n) is constant densities with coefficients summing to zero, giving E/K isometrically. If an L-arc exists, diagonal limits of norm-minimizing corrections may lose scalar mass; depositing precisely that mass on the L-arc recovers a minimal lift. Dyadic signs on all arc components tend weakly to zero by the Rademacher lemma and dominated ell1 summation, while admissible mean-zero derivative tests force quotient perturbation norm to 1; signed norms tend to 1. If no L-arc exists, endpoint molecule has finite-coordinate dual slack, which forces every finitely truncated zero-mean projection of a hypothetical almost-square weak-null sequence to vanish. Uniform tails for weak-null ell1-sum sequences plus the scalar endpoint coordinate then force its entire norm to vanish, contradiction. All-vector/unbounded lengths and metric boundaries covered; analytic proof, no finite tests.
